resources.string: How T cells mature in the thymus
One typical route for conventional T cells in a human thymic lobule. Cell numbers, sizes and timing are schematic.
The thymus sits behind the breastbone. Early T-cell precursors arrive in the blood near the boundary between the cortex and medulla, then move into the outer cortex.

Cortical epithelial cells display protein fragments on self MHC molecules. Developing T cells survive positive selection if their receptors receive a suitable signal from this display. Too little signal means they do not survive.
Selected cells move toward the medulla
After positive selection, developing T cells move inward from the outer cortex toward the medulla, where they continue to mature.
In the medulla, developing T cells encounter a wider range of self peptides. Cells that react too strongly are generally removed, although some become regulatory T cells.
Mature naive T cells leave the thymus and enter the blood. They have matured but are not yet activated. Activation is a separate step that can occur later outside the thymus.
